messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications & next steps (Aurora Tech)

Hi Laura 

thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on: 

1) Controller vs Processor: You asked how we reflect roles in the DPA. Per standard practice, Redwood is the processor when we process customer-provided data on your behalf. We will send the DPA (attached) with the processor language in Section 2. 

2) Subprocessors: I attached our current subprocessor list (CSV). If you need a separate CSM/legal call to review the list and any objections, happy to set that up. 

3) Breach notice timeline: Our standard is to notify customers without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects customer data. We can discuss SLA language if you require different timing.

4) Data residency & retention: We support US and EU region tenancy. For Aurora I noted you prefer US-only residency; we can configure dedicated tenancy for the production environments in us-west. Retention policies can be configured per workspace 







— typical defaults are 30/90/365 days depending on logs vs. persistent storage.

Next steps I propose: 
- Share DPA + subprocessor list (attached) 




— ACTION: Marissa (done)
- Schedule a 30-min legal call to review any DPA redlines 

— ACTION: Laura to propose times
- Provide SOC 2 report and optional KMS/HSM details 
— ACTION: Ben to attach SOC 2 link in follow-up

If that looks right, can we aim to get the redlines from your legal team by EOD Friday so we can keep the timeline for onboarding next quarter?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@auroratech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Tech Legal <legal@auroratech.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & next steps (Aurora Tech)

Hi Marissa 

thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from our legal/privacy team: 

- Controller/Processor: We operate as the controller for customer data we collect and provide. Does Redwood accept processor-only obligations in the DPA or do you require any controller-level commitments? Please confirm the exact language you use for processor responsibilities (section and paragraph would help).

- Subprocessors: We need a timed notification window whenever you add a new subprocessor and the ability to object for a limited period. What's your change-notice process today and how long do customers have to object?

- Breach notice: The 72-hour window is noted. Our policy is that any confirmed breach affecting PII requires notice within 48 hours. Is Redwood willing to commit to 48 hours for confirmed breaches? If not, can we map the trigger (e.g., "confirmed compromise of customer data") to ensure alignment?

- Data residency: We prefer all production inference and logs remain in US-based regions only. What operational controls and contractual guarantees do you provide to ensure no backups or logs are replicated to EU hosts?

- Data retention & deletion: We need a contractual retention schedule and confirmation that upon termination you will delete or return customer data within 30 days unless otherwise agreed. Can you confirm?

We expect to get an initial redline back to you by next Wednesday at the latest, but want to confirm these points before scheduling a conversation with our outside counsel.

Best,
Laura Jensen
Head of Platform Security, Aurora Tech
laura.jensen@auroratech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@auroratech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & next steps (Aurora Tech)

Hi Laura 


thanks, really helpful questions. See answers inline below and next steps at the end. I've also looped in Ben (Security & Compliance) and Dev (Solutions Engineer) for technical details / SOC docs.

- Controller/Processor: Redwood will execute the DPA as Processor. The DPA's Section 2 ("Roles and Responsibilities") specifies processor obligations including only processing per documented instructions, implementing technical and organizational measures, and assisting with data subject requests. If Aurora needs additional "controller-like" assurances (e.g., obligations around lawful basis), we can add clarifying language but typically remain in the processor role contractually.

- Subprocessors: We provide a published subprocessor list and notify customers via email + portal announcement at least 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor. Customers have a 14-day window to object; if a substantive objection is raised we will discuss mitigation (e.g., alternative controls or, in rare cases, remove the subprocessor for that customer). We can include this timeline in the DPA.

- Breach notice: Our standard is notification without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of confirming a security incident. I hear Aurora's 48-hour requirement — I'll flag that to our security leadership as an exception request. Can you share whether 48 hours is a hard contractual requirement or a preference for faster notification? That will help when I escalate.

- Data residency: For production tenancy we can ensure inference compute and primary logs remain in us-west region. We will commit in contract that backups and replicas for your tenancy will not be stored outside the US unless you opt in. Operationally, we can set the tenancy region and enforce network egress rules; Dev can confirm how we isolate logs and backups for a dedicated tenancy.

- Data retention & deletion: We support configurable retention policies. Default approach: on contract termination we will delete customer data within 30 days, unless you request extended archival. We'll include the 30-day deletion clause in Section 7 of the DPA by default, with the option to change by mutual agreement.

Next steps:
- I'll escalate the 48-hour breach notice request to Security (Ben) 

— ACTION: Ben to confirm whether we can contractually support 48 hours or provide an agreed trigger.
- Dev to share SOC 2 link and KMS/HSM configuration notes 

— ACTION: Dev
- If Aurora can share any specific DPA redlines, we'll review and set a legal call for next week.

Ben/Dev 

— can you please attach SOC2 report and the subprocessor details (technical controls) in your replies?

Thanks,
Marissa
